Repo: gazebosim/gz-transport, branch gz-transport13 (Harmonic)

## Summary

UDP discovery treats the two halves of the pub/sub rendezvous asymmetrically:

- **ADVERTISE is self-healing**: re-broadcast every heartbeat cycle in `Discovery.hh UpdateHeartbeat()` ("Re-advertise topics that are advertised inside this process").
- **Subscription registration is fire-and-forget**: when the subscriber's node discovers a new publisher, `NodeShared.cc OnNewConnection()` sends `msgDiscovery->Register(pub)` exactly once per local handler:

  ```cpp
  for (const std::string &nodeUuid : handlerNodeUuids)
  {
    pub.SetNUuid(nodeUuid);
    // Send a message to the publisher notify it
    // about all my remoteSubscribers.
    this->dataPtr->msgDiscovery->Register(pub);
  }
  ```

  There is no ACK, no retry loop, and heartbeats do not replay it.

- **The publisher side has no recovery path**: `remoteSubscribers.AddPublisher(_pub)` happens only when a Register datagram arrives (`OnNewRegistration`). Entries are never aged out, and `OnNewConnection` is gated on a *new* connection — for an already-connected topic the heartbeat ADVERTISE never re-triggers the Register send.

Net effect: if the single Register datagram is lost (discovery socket buffer overflow, receiver CPU starvation — classic during N-host concurrent boot), both sides look healthy afterwards (ZMQ TCP connected, publisher keeps publishing), but `Publish()` skips that subscriber **forever, silently**.

## Real-world impact (PX4 SITL fleet, gz-transport13 / Harmonic)

We operate PX4 SITL + Gazebo with many vehicles sharing one network namespace (`net=host`), all booting concurrently. During an 8-vehicle concurrent boot, 50–100% of vehicles randomly lost one sensor-topic family at the PX4 consumer side (accel / mag / baro / gps — a different family each time): the gz side kept publishing, the bridge's subscriber sockets stayed connected, and the topic simply never arrived. Single-vehicle starts never reproduced it.

Mitigations that made 8/8 boots clean — both consistent with "the one-shot Register is the single point of failure":

1. Per-instance discovery plane: `GZ_DISCOVERY_MSG_PORT` / `GZ_DISCOVERY_SRV_PORT` offset per instance (removes cross-host beacon/Register flooding on the shared multicast channel).
2. Deferring a local 3×4 MB/s MAVLink injection burst until after the first seconds of boot (removes same-host CPU/socket pressure on the Register window).
3. A watchdog that polls the consumer side (`listener`) and restarts the whole container on a missing family — because nothing in gz-transport itself ever retries or heals the lost registration.

## Possible directions

1. Replay SUBSCRIBE/Register alongside the ADVERTISE heartbeat (late/lost registrations self-heal within one cycle), or
2. Publisher-side aging of `remoteSubscribers` + subscriber-side periodic re-Register, or
3. An ACK-based registration handshake.

Happy to provide more traces/details if useful.
new_candidates.title: Subscription registration is fire-and-forget: one lost Register datagram during discovery churn permanently (and silently) starves the topic
